question_text:
Calculate the maximum internal crack length allowable for a Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy ( table 9.1 ) component that is loaded to a stress one-half its yield strength. Assume that the value of $Y$ is 1.50 .

Reference:
"Table 9.1
Room-Temperature Yield Strength and Plane Strain Fracture Toughness Data for Selected Engineering Materials
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|l|l|}
\hline \multirow[b]{2}{*}{Material} & \multicolumn{2}{|c|}{Yield Strength} & \multicolumn{2}{|c|}{$\boldsymbol{K}_{\boldsymbol{I} \boldsymbol{c}}$} \\
\hline & MPa & ksi & $\mathrm{MPa} \sqrt{\mathrm{m}}$ & ksi $\sqrt{\text { in. }}$ \\
\hline \multicolumn{5}{|c|}{Metals} \\
\hline Aluminum alloy ${ }^a$ (7075-T651) & 495 & 72 & 24 & 22 \\
\hline Aluminum alloy ${ }^a$ (2024-T3) & 345 & 50 & 44 & 40 \\
\hline Titanium alloy ${ }^a$ (Ti-6Al-4V) & 910 & 132 & 55 & 50 \\
\hline Alloy steel ${ }^a$ (4340 tempered @ $260^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ ) & 1640 & 238 & 50.0 & 45.8 \\
\hline Alloy steel ${ }^a$ ( 4340 tempered @ $425{ }^{\circ}$ C) & 1420 & 206 & 87.4 & 80.0 \\
\hline \multicolumn{5}{|c|}{Ceramics} \\
\hline Concrete & - & - & 0.2-1.4 & 0.18-1.27 \\
\hline Soda-lime glass & - & - & 0.7-0.8 & 0.64-0.73 \\
\hline Aluminum oxide & - & - & 2.7-5.0 & 2.5-4.6 \\
\hline & \multicolumn{4}{|l|}{Polymers} \\
\hline Polystyrene (PS) & 25.0-69.0 & 3.63-10.0 & 0.7-1.1 & 0.64-1.0 \\
\hline Poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) & 53.8-73.1 & 7.8-10.6 & 0.7-1.6 & 0.64-1.5 \\
\hline Polycarbonate (PC) & 62.1 & 9.0 & 2.2 & 2.0 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}"The unit of the answer is mm.
